question: In paediatric practice, functional constipation is a clinical diagnosis based on ROME IV criteria and does NOT require a rectal biopsy for routine diagnosis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Functional constipation = clinical diagnosis (ROME IV). Rectal biopsy (for absence of ganglion cells) is only needed when Hirschsprung disease is suspected — absent meconium in first 48 h of life, empty rectum on examination, or features not fitting functional constipation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Functional constipation is diagnosed clinically using ROME IV criteria (e.g. ≤2 stools/week, painful defecation, faecal incontinence, large-calibre stools, impaction). Rectal biopsy is reserved for suspected Hirschsprung disease — characterised by failure to pass meconium within 48 h, empty rectum on examination, and explosive release of stool on withdrawal of the finger.
